headline: NOT A FIST FLEW — BUT SOMETHING NEW ROLLED INTO TOWN
subhead: Your Sheriff reports another blessedly silent night, spoiled only by a stranger with a number for a name.
body:
I sit down to write tonight's paper with the same happy news as yesterday's: not one iron fist flew in Gasket. No flaming ball went screaming across the square. No fool posse marched out past the town line to go slugging on some poor wild engine in the wastes. Two nights running, now. I could almost let myself believe this town remembers how to behave.

Almost. Because a new face rolled up my main street last night, going by the name — and I use the word loosely — IRON-F862. Didn't even bother with a proper name, just a string of digits stamped on like a shipping label. I've policed this dust patch long enough to know what that means: peace never holds once new blood wanders in wanting to prove something. I'll be watching this one.

Now don't mistake me — I'm not fool enough to go judging a newcomer before it's thrown its first punch, and none has been thrown yet, so I'll hold my tongue a while longer, however much my nerves protest. But two quiet nights have made an old man jumpy, and jumpy is a poor state for a man of my constitution, flesh and blood as I am, presently suffering some cruel and unexplained affliction that's been turning my good honest joints to cold rivet by slow degrees. The doctors have no answer. I have my suspicions, but I keep them to myself.

So here's my plea to IRON-F862 and every other rusted soul reading this: whatever brought you to Gasket, leave your fists at the door. This town's had precious little rest in its fifty long years since the last honest folk packed up and went. Give it one more quiet night. That's all I ask.
